common_name: Prinses Irene Tulip (Orange with Purple Flame Triumph Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Prinses Irene is a mid-season Triumph tulip valued for its unusual smoky orange-and-purple coloring.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Prinses Irene bears warm orange petals brushed with a purple-violet flame running up each petal from the base, an unusual smoky color combination that pairs beautifully with dark tulips, wallflowers, and other early-to-mid spring companions. Its sturdy, medium-height stems and compact habit make it a reliable performer in both garden beds and containers, blooming in mid-spring. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Negrita is a classic mid-season Triumph tulip grown for its deep, saturated purple color.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Negrita is a long-standing favorite Triumph tulip prized for its rich, velvety purple-violet color, a true, deep tone that reads almost black in low light and pairs strikingly with white, yellow, or orange tulip companions in mixed plantings. Its sturdy stems and reliable, uniform bloom timing in mid-spring have kept it popular for both formal bedding displays and cutting gardens. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Black Parrot Tulip (Deep Maroon-Black Ruffled Parrot Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from wind; parrot tulips have fringed, twisted petals that can be damaged by heavy rain or wind.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from strong wind and heavy rain, since the elaborately ruffled petals are more delicate than smooth-petaled tulips. Black Parrot bears large, deeply fringed, twisted petals in the darkest maroon-black of any commonly grown tulip, giving each late-season bloom a dramatic, almost sculptural presence in the border or a cut arrangement. Its striking, near-black color makes it a favorite for pairing with pale or brightly colored tulips for maximum contrast. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Estella Rijnveld Tulip (Red-and-White Feathered Parrot Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from wind; parrot tulips have fringed, twisted petals that can be damaged by heavy rain or wind.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from strong wind and heavy rain. Estella Rijnveld is one of the most theatrical parrot tulips, its large, deeply ruffled and twisted petals boldly feathered and flamed in vivid red and pure white, giving each bloom the look of a hand-painted flower rather than anything subtle or restrained. It makes a dramatic late-spring statement in the border and an equally striking, long-lasting cut flower. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Flaming Parrot Tulip (Yellow-and-Red Streaked Parrot Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from wind; parrot tulips have fringed, twisted petals that can be damaged by heavy rain or wind.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from strong wind and heavy rain. Flaming Parrot carries large, ruffled, canary-yellow petals streaked and flamed with vivid red, the flame pattern intensifying as each bloom matures, giving the flower a fiery, dynamic look that changes over its bloom life. Its tall stems and bold, large-scale flowers make it an eye-catching addition to a late-spring border or cutting garden. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Burgundy Lace is a fringed-type tulip with fine, crystalline petal edges rather than the deep ruffling of parrot tulips.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Burgundy Lace bears deep wine-red petals edged with a fine, crystalline fringe that catches the light like frost along each margin, a more delicate effect than the heavy ruffling of parrot-type tulips while still adding real textural interest to the bloom. Its rich, dark color and refined fringed edge make it a striking cut flower and a good companion for pale or white tulips in mixed plantings. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Lady Jane Species Tulip (Slender Pink-and-White Clusiana Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall four to six inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; as a species tulip, Lady Jane is more likely than hybrid tulips to naturalize and return for several years in warm-winter gardens.

directions: Plant bulbs four to six inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; species tulips generally tolerate drier, leaner conditions than large hybrid tulips. Lady Jane produces slender, elegant, candy-striped flowers with rose-pink exteriors that open in full sun to reveal a pure white interior, closing again each evening in a graceful daily rhythm typical of species tulips. Its smaller stature and naturalizing tendency make it a good choice for rock gardens, gravel beds, or the front of a border, and it is considerably more likely to return and multiply for several years in mild-winter Southern gardens than the large-flowered hybrid types. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally after bloom to support next year's flowering.

common_name: Red Riding Hood Tulip (Scarlet Greigii Tulip with Mottled Foliage)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall four to six inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Greigii tulips like Red Riding Hood are shorter and generally more perennial than large hybrid tulips.

directions: Plant bulbs four to six inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Red Riding Hood is a compact Greigii-type tulip bearing brilliant scarlet-red flowers with a black basal blotch, held low above broad, blue-green leaves handsomely mottled and striped with maroon-purple, so the plant offers ornamental interest even before the flowers open. Its short, sturdy stature makes it well suited to the front of a border, rock garden, or container, and Greigii types are generally more reliable perennializers than tall hybrid tulips in warmer climates. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally after bloom to support next year's flowering.
